Text:
One single continuous photograph — no panels, grids, or split frames.

Use the uploaded photo as the exact base composition. The street in the source
is empty — populate it with the people and vehicles specified below. Remove all
modern businesses, logos, brands, storefront names, banners, advertisements, and
signage visible in the source image.

PRESERVE (must match source exactly)
- camera: eye-level, street-facing, fov 80
- main street road, 2-lane, asphalt
- sidewalks present, curbs present
- driveways: alley entrance mid-block; parking: parallel street parking both sides
- two-story brick commercial building at left block face, 2 stories, red brick, cast iron storefront columns, flat parapet roof, at sidewalk setback
- single-story retail building at center block face, 1 story, brick, plate glass storefront, flat with low parapet roof, at sidewalk setback
- corner mixed-use building at right corner, 3 stories, brick, stone trim cornice, flat roof, at sidewalk setback
- utilities: overhead power and telephone lines, wooden utility poles every 50 feet
- landscape: concrete sidewalks, brick pavers at crosswalks, small planted tree pits
- immutable elements: cast iron storefront columns on left building, recessed corner entrance on right building, brick alley mid-block
Keep this location instantly recognizable.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Create a TRUE 9:16 vertical portrait. Expand the SAME scene naturally above
(sky) and below (street/pavement) as canvas extension — do not stretch or
distort the source geometry.

TRANSFORM TO 1975
Post-Vietnam, oil crisis era. A working small-town main street in 1975 — locally owned shops with hand-painted and neon signs, a five & dime, and not a single modern chain in sight.

CONDITION: new — recently built appearance, pristine surfaces, new signage

PERIOD DETAILS
- TOWN DINER with a hand-lettered 'HOT COFFEE 25¢' sign in the window
- 'HOME APPLIANCE CO' window displaying console televisions with a 'COLOR TV' placard
- 'WOOLWORTH' five & dime with red-and-white lettering
- window signs: 'SHIRTS 2 FOR $5', 'HAIRCUT $2.50'
- a painted ghost-sign wall advertisement on brick, weathered but still clearly readable
- a glass-and-aluminum telephone booth on the corner
Typography: bold sans-serif, slab serif, occasional script.
Sign text is only what appears in quotes — do not turn other words from this prompt into signage.

PEOPLE
EXACTLY 30 people TOTAL: 12 near sidewalk (largest, foreground), 11 opposite sidewalk mid-block, 7 distant, far end of block. Grouped in pairs, threes, and singles.
- a barber visible through the shop window cutting hair
- two men in short-sleeve dress shirts talking outside the hardware store
- a shopkeeper in an apron by his doorway
Clothing: men in turtlenecks, wide lapels; women in wide leg pants, earth tones. No posing or eye contact. All people stay on sidewalks, at storefronts, or beside parked vehicles — never standing, sitting, or walking in the road or driving lanes.

VEHICLES
EXACTLY 4 period vehicles, all different:
- 1973-1980 Chevrolet C10 — square body, chrome bumper
- 1971-1976 Jeep Wagoneer — boxy full-size SUV, woodgrain trim optional
- 1970-1978 AMC Gremlin — short stubby hatchback rear
- 1974-1978 Cadillac DeVille — full-size luxury, formal roofline, chrome heavy
Parked with gaps; no vehicle newer than 1975.
Parked vehicles hug the curb — parallel, each facing its lane's direction; none sideways, diagonal, or against traffic. Keep at least one full driving lane clear each way for through traffic.
PLACEMENT: the first one parked on the LEFT side near the corner; the rest parked on the RIGHT side. No vehicle in the same spot as any other era.

ENVIRONMENT
- road markings: yellow center line, white edge lines, no rumble strips
- utilities: overhead power lines everywhere, wooden utility poles standard

TREES
- oak tree at sidewalk left near corner: clearly smaller than in the source — about 60% of its canopy there, thinner trunk
- maple tree at sidewalk center in front of retail: a young tree, only about 30% of its canopy in the source photo, thin trunk
Tree sizes MUST follow this specification even where they differ from the source photo.

PHOTOGRAPHIC STYLE
STRICTLY BLACK AND WHITE — true monochrome archival photograph, zero color anywhere.
Grain: visible fine grain. Style: documentary, natural light.
Photorealistic, like a preserved newspaper-archive frame; slight period-lens softness, not digitally sharp.

PRIVACY
Blur all faces and license plates.
SelectedVehicles: 1973-1980 Chevrolet C10 — square body, chrome bumper
1971-1976 Jeep Wagoneer — boxy full-size SUV, woodgrain trim optional
1970-1978 AMC Gremlin — short stubby hatchback rear
1974-1978 Cadillac DeVille — full-size luxury, formal roofline, chrome heavy
